title: Data is everything
blurb: AI learns from data — pick the right measurements and make the first cut that separates the kinds.

steps.title: What data looks like
steps.body:
An AI learns from a big pile of **examples** — that's **data**, usually just a **table**. Each **row** is one example (one penguin, one photo). Each **column** is one thing we measured.

Two words pros use constantly:
- **Features** = the things we *measure* (a penguin's bill length, flipper length…).
- **Label** = the *answer* we want (which kind of penguin it is).

The AI's job: look at the **features** and guess the **label**.

steps.title: Make the first cut
steps.body: Here are two kinds of penguin with three measurements each. Put measurements on the **X** and **Y** axes, then **drag the divider** to split the two kinds apart. Find the measurements + cut that separate them best — aim for 90%.

steps.title: Good features do the work
steps.body:
Notice how **some measurements separated the penguins cleanly** and others left the colors all mixed up? Picking **good features** is half the battle in real AI.

It's like guessing someone's favorite sport: their *height* helps a little, but "do they own a soccer ball?" helps a lot more. With the right features, a single cut already does most of the job — that's the seed of every classifier.

steps.title: Garbage in, garbage out — and bias
steps.body:
Here's the rule behind most AI failures: **an AI can only be as good as its data.** Messy or lopsided data → a confused AI.

Imagine training on **100 of one kind and 4 of the other**. The AI barely sees the rare kind, so it just guesses the common one — not because it's smart, but because that's mostly what it *saw*. That lopsidedness has a name: **bias**, and it comes from the data we collect, not the computer.

steps.title: Spot the bias
steps.question: An AI that sorts fruit was trained on 100 apples and 4 bananas. What will probably happen?
choices: It leans toward guessing 'apple' because that's mostly what it saw
steps.explain: Exactly — a lopsided dataset makes a lopsided AI. Balanced, fair examples are the fix, and that's one of the most important jobs in real AI.

steps.title: What you learned 🎉
steps.body:
- **Data** = a table of examples with **features** (what we measure) and a **label** (the answer)
- **Good features** make the kinds separate — you found them and cut them apart yourself
- **Garbage in, garbage out** — data quality beats computer speed
- **Bias** is born from lopsided data; **balanced, fair data** is the cure

**Next up:** instead of sorting into kinds, you'll teach an AI to **predict a number** — that's *regression*.
